rationale: Both use the traffic x conversion x order-value driver framework with side-by-side tables and bottom-up, scenario-based tips. A contributes returns-rate netting, inventory and stockout constraints, and an omnichannel attribution note. However, it has some shaky claims: in-store tickets are said to be lower because of impulse buys, a ski-shop versus beachwear example is confusing, and its granularity row is contradictory. B offers sharper, more decision-relevant insights. It contrasts typical conversion rates (20-40% in-store versus 1-3% online) and notes diminishing returns and rising CAC as ad spend scales. It covers trade-area modelling, competitor-radius effects, ramp curves for new stores and store-level weather effects, plus the email list as a controllable lever. It adds methodological advice A lacks: reconcile top-down against bottom-up, and track forecast error (MAPE, bias) by driver so you know which assumption is off. B is somewhat more accurate and insightful.
